issue_context.title: Setting number of digits for verisure PIN does not take effect until after restart
issue_context.body:
### The problem

When changing the number of digits in the Verisure pin code, the new setting does not take effect until HA is restarted.

So changing it from e.g 4 to 6 still gives you the error about a correct pin not matching regexp \d{4}, until after HA restart.

The problem is most probably here:
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/804b27cc2fd470c6f0c52609ef21f5ca540f4386/homeassistant/components/verisure/config_flow.py#L318

Where, if I understand this correctly, the config entry is updated, but the running entity is not updated.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2023.6.3

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

Verisure

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/verisure/

review_comments: I didn't check but typically we just reload the config entry to load new settings.

Yes, that also works here, but that is a much heavier operation, including triggering an extra call to fetch data from Verisure, which are (as I understand it) rate limiting their API quite strict. In this way, we avoid that extra external request when only updating local configuration. I checked a few different integrations, and some reloads, while others do not. Perhaps I am suboptimisng here?

(What I actually found  a bit strange, was that the lock entity fetches `code_format` on update, and not when opening the options flow in the UI.)
Not sure I understand the last sentence?

> Not sure I understand the last sentence?

When debugging, I noticed that `code_format()` was called about once a minute, apparently after data is received from Verisure.
That's not important for this PR though. I am happy to change to reload the config entry if that's the preferred way.

No, I'm now wondering if the `update_listener` even have to do anything since `code_format` is only used for the services and frontend which I think is reading live.
You ticked the box but have you tested this?

Yes, of course I tested this :)

Without `update_listener`, the code_format in the OptionsFlow is not updated until after the next data fetching. Here is with added logging in `code_format()` in `verisure/lock.py`:

```

```

